content.text: Look through the code and issues and lets figure out what to work on next. Make sure to use AGENTS.md

I’ll use the repository’s `plan-and-prototype` guidance to choose a thin, shippable slice, and the GitHub skill to inspect the live roadmap, issues, and PR state. I’ll first establish the current worktree/instructions and use the relevant prior project notes only as leads; current code and GitHub state will decide the recommendation.

The checkout is clean on `main`, with local `main` matching the currently recorded `origin/main`. The prior note says the roadmap moved forward substantially and specifically warns that parent issue checkboxes can lag implementation, so I’m treating it only as a search hint. I’m now reconciling live milestones/issues/PRs against the code that actually landed.

Live priority is now unambiguous: Phase 2 has exactly one open roadmap item, [#77](https://github.com/scottdensmore/travel-app/issues/77), and there are no open pull requests. However, the recent history shows two check-in slices already landed, so I’m reading the issue’s remaining contract and the actual check-in policy/UI/database paths before naming the next slice.

The key dependency is real, and the smallest safe policy is starting to emerge: keep seat changes available before check-in, but freeze a traveler’s seat once that leg is checked in and a pass can exist. That avoids silently “reissuing” an artifact without any version or delivery contract, while preserving the later #77 slice for choosing seats inside the check-in journey. I’m checking whether the existing checkout “e-ticket” can be cleanly reused or needs a dedicated owner-scoped projection.

The code settles the architecture without a spike: `SeatAssignment` already provides the traveler–leg identity, seat/cabin, and `checkedInAt` issuance time; `Booking.reference` and flight/route data are already persisted. So the boarding-pass slice needs no schema migration or dependency. The checkout card is only visual prior art—it is transient “E‑Ticket” UI created immediately after purchase, not a retrievable check-in artifact.

## Recommendation

Work next on [#77: check-in and travel documents](https://github.com/scottdensmore/travel-app/issues/77), specifically:

> Generate owner-scoped boarding passes, while resolving [#312](https://github.com/scottdensmore/travel-app/issues/312) by freezing seats after check-in.

This is the right priority because Phase 2 has exactly one open issue, there are no open PRs or assignees, and `main` is clean and synchronized with GitHub at `d70cd0e`.

Why this slice is ready:

- #314 delivered eligibility and check-in.
- #315 delivered document attestation.
- The check-in query is already owner-scoped and loads the necessary traveler, flight, seat, cabin, reference, and check-in data in [app/checkin/page.tsx](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/travel-app/app/checkin/page.tsx:96).
- `SeatAssignment` already represents one traveler on one leg and includes `checkedInAt`, so no migration or dependency is required: [prisma/schema.prisma](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/travel-app/prisma/schema.prisma:624).
- The existing checkout “boarding pass” is transient pre-check-in E‑Ticket UI with a decorative fake barcode. It is visual prior art, not a persisted, retrievable check-in artifact: [BookingCheckoutWizard.tsx](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/travel-app/components/ui/BookingCheckoutWizard.tsx:1748).
- Seat changes currently rewrite `seatNumber` without checking `checkedInAt`, which is precisely #312: [app/actions.ts](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/travel-app/app/actions.ts:1127).

### Seat policy decision

| Option | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Freeze seats after check-in | Recommended. Small, fail-closed, and keeps every issued pass stable. |
| Automatically reissue | Needs artifact versioning, delivery behavior, and audit semantics. Too broad now. |
| Record pass revisions | Strongest long-term auditability, but requires a new model and migration. |

The later “allowed seat changes at check-in” slice can still let customers choose a seat before the final check-in action.

### Thin implementation slice

1. Start with failing product tests proving a checked-in leg cannot have its seats changed, including contention with check-in under the flight lock.
2. Project one boarding pass per checked-in, currently travelling passenger and leg from persisted data.
3. Render passes on `/checkin` after success and on later visits, with confirmation, traveler, route, flight, departure, cabin, seat, and check-in time.
4. Keep the server query owner-scoped and prove another authenticated user cannot retrieve the passes.
5. Update the profile seat-change UI to omit or clearly explain checked-in legs, while keeping un-checked legs changeable.
6. Exercise multi-passenger and round-trip behavior end to end.

Deliberately deferred: choosing seats inside check-in, email/resend delivery, and receipt work. Those remain separate #77 slices.

No prototype is needed—the current schema establishes feasibility. No files were changed and no test gate was run during this read-only triage. The prior project notes were used only as search leads; the recommendation above was revalidated against live GitHub and current `main`.
